title: Coursebook frequency inventory v1
description: A frequency inventory is a declared, immutable, ranked list of lexical items for exactly one language and one declared modality. Frequency ranks are corpus- and modality-specific: a rank from a written-newspaper corpus does not order spoken conversation, and no rank or band in this document is a comprehension percentage or evidence that a learner knows a share of the language. Coursebook bundles no third-party frequency list; this contract describes a user- or pack-supplied import, and the only bundled document is an explicitly synthetic test fixture. A row's `band` must name a declared band and its `rank` must fall inside that band's rank range; every rank from 1 to the row count belongs to exactly one band. Rows whose part of speech is `particle`, `copula`, `auxiliary` or `conjunction` are grammatical items: a plan must teach them as grammar in context and must not name them as vocabulary targets.
x-frequency-note: A frequency rank orders items inside the corpus and modality that produced it. It is not a comprehension percentage. 80% token coverage is not comprehension; 95-98% coverage is the useful reading/listening target, and only when a cited source supports that band. Kanji frequency is a separate problem from word frequency and is out of scope for this contract.
x-bundling-rule: Only `redistribution: allowed` inventories whose licence is CC0-1.0, public-domain, CC-BY-4.0 or CC-BY-SA-4.0 may be bundled with the plugin. CC-BY-NC-* and all-rights-reserved lists may be imported by a user into their own workspace but never shipped. The repository currently carries no outbound licence, so no third-party inventory may be bundled here yet.

modality.description: The modality of the corpus the ranks were counted from. `mixed` means the source aggregates modalities and cannot be attributed to one of them.

tokenization.description: How the corpus was segmented into the listed lemmas, and on what unit the rank counts (for example UniDic short units, MeCab+IPADIC, or hand-authored fixture rows).

scope_note.description: What the ranks do and do not claim for this list. Must not present coverage as comprehension.

content_hash.description: sha256 over the canonical JSON of the rows array exactly as shipped: UTF-8, keys sorted, no insignificant whitespace.
